bib.title: In-Context Learning with Long-Context Models: An In-Depth Exploration

question: How does in-context learning behave when the context holds hundreds to thousands of demonstrations, and how does it compare with retrieval and finetuning?
hypothesis: Long-context ICL is beneficial mainly because attention retrieves relevant examples, not because demonstrations are contextualized with each other.
contributions: ICL performance keeps rising with thousands of demonstrations on large-label-space datasets
Comparison with example retrieval and with full and LoRA finetuning
Properties: less order sensitivity, harm from label grouping, benefit not from cumulative encoding (block-attention tests)

method.summary: ICL with up to ~2000 demonstrations on five classification datasets and SAMSum, using Llama-2 variants (4k, 32k, 80k), Mistral-7b and Qwen2.5-7B, compared with BM25/BERTScore-Recall retrieval ICL and finetuning of Llama2-7b with a classification head (full and LoRA). Block-sparse attention masks test whether demonstrations need long-range attention.

datasets.name: NLU
datasets.preprocessing: all 68 intents used; avg demo length 20.7

datasets.name: Clinic-150
datasets.preprocessing: 'plus' train split with extra out-of-scope; avg demo length 22.3

datasets.name: SAMSum
datasets.preprocessing: avg demo length 167.9; outliers in top 1% of demo length discarded in stats

other.use: Clinic-150, 50 to 3000 demos, via Anthropic API

models.name: Llama2-7b + classification head (finetuned)
models.init_from: Llama-2-7b; head initialised from LM head subsampled at first token of each label

training.epochs: 30 epochs, evaluated every epoch; best test-accuracy checkpoint chosen
training.seeds: several random seeds (5 seeds in Fig 15; 3 seeds in Fig 16)

other.tuning: hyperparameters tuned only on Banking-77; full-FT hyperparameters not stated
other.model_selection: uses the test set, which favours finetuning

inference.decoding: constrained decoding to valid labels (large constant added to valid-label logits, following Ratner et al. 2022); none for frontier models
inference.samples: 10 random shuffles of the training set averaged; first n examples of each shuffle; 3 shuffles for order-sensitivity and BM25 shuffle tests; frontier models single run
inference.prompting: Input/output prefixes with '==' separators, no instruction or system prompt; k up to ~2000 demonstrations
inference.retrieval: BM25 (stopwords removed) or BERTScore-Recall, query = test input vs full demo text; random fill if fewer than k retrieved

parameters.block_attention: 1 sink block + 2 local blocks, block size b (50 in ablation); test example attends to all demos
parameters.ICL_100_to_2000: context lengths capped at each model's trained context

other.cache_note: random set can be encoded once and cached

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: classification accuracy on 250 subsampled test examples

metrics.name: % labels flipped
metrics.definition: share of predictions that change under reordering

eval.protocol: 250 test examples per dataset; 2-sided t-test p<0.05 for shuffling and short-context comparisons; saturation = smallest n reaching 95% of max accuracy

availability.data: subsampled test sets and full predictions released in the repository

evidence.quote: We note that using the test set to perform model selection presents an unfair advantage to finetuning

results.claim: Scaling from 10 to 1000 demonstrations raises accuracy by up to 50.8 points.
results.setup: 5 classification datasets, random-selection ICL, Llama2-7b variants/Mistral/Qwen; 250 test examples each; 10 shuffles; constrained decoding
results.quote: Scaling up from 10 to 1000 demonstrations results in accuracy gains of up to 50.8 points (and an average of 36.8 points across 5 datasets for Llama2-80k).

results.claim: Average gain from 10 to 1000 demos for Llama2-80k across the 5 datasets.
results.setup: Llama2-80k, 5 classification datasets, random ICL, 10 to 1000 demos
results.quote: Scaling up from 10 to 1000 demonstrations results in accuracy gains of up to 50.8 points (and an average of 36.8 points across 5 datasets for Llama2-80k).

results.claim: BM25 retrieval gain over random selection on Banking-77 shrinks from 51.5 points at 1 shot to 4.9 at 1500 shot.
results.setup: Banking-77, BM25 vs random selection; the sentence does not name the model (Fig 12/Table 2 show several)
results.quote: On Banking-77, the dataset where retrieval is most beneficial, the performance gain from BM25 retrieval drops from 51.5 points at 1-shot ICL to 4.9 points at 1500-shot ICL.
results.note: Model for the 51.5/4.9 figures is not stated in the sentence.

results.claim: Using one random demonstration set instead of retrieval costs at most 5 points at the longest contexts.
results.setup: longest context regime studied, random vs retrieval, 7B models
results.quote: the performance penalty for doing so is never more than 5 points, and as low as 1.8 points (in 2000-shot ICL on TREC).

results.claim: Smallest random-vs-retrieval penalty: 1.8 points at 2000-shot on TREC.
results.quote: the performance penalty for doing so is never more than 5 points, and as low as 1.8 points (in 2000-shot ICL on TREC).

results.claim: Label sorting lowers accuracy by 25.7 points at 1169-shot.
results.setup: Llama2-32k, Clinic-150, examples sorted by label vs original (random) order
results.quote: at 1169-shot ICL, label sorting decreases accuracy by 25.7 percentage points.

results.claim: Share of labels flipped by random reshuffling at 1000-shot is under half that at 10-shot.
results.quote: Across all datasets, the percent of labels flipped by shuffling in 1000-shot ICL is less than half the percentage flipped in 10-shot ICL.

results.claim: Performance is monotonic on nearly every dataset; the full context is not harmful.
results.quote: However, we observe monotonically increasing performance on nearly every dataset

results.claim: Block attention with a 50-example block recovers 95% of full attention on Banking-77.
results.setup: Llama2-32k, Banking-77, k fixed, block size b varied; sink block plus two local blocks
results.quote: 95% of the performance of full attention is recovered by a block of 50 examples in the case of Banking-77

results.claim: Block sizes below 10 give near-zero performance.
results.quote: using block sizes b < 10 results in near-zero performance

results.claim: Chosen attention mask (1 sink + 2 local blocks, b=50) gets 77.51 accuracy vs 80.04 for full causal at 500 demos.
results.note: Two tables are numbered Table 6: the main-text reference to 'Table 6' for ICL results is Table 2.

results.claim: Attention-mask ablation: only the current block gives 18.72 accuracy.
results.setup: Llama2-80k, Banking-77, b=50, 500 demos, no sink, no local blocks

results.claim: One local block plus sink recovers 94% of full-attention performance.
results.quote: although one local block is sufficient to recover 94% of the performance of the full attention method

results.claim: Finetuning (full) with far more examples than fit in-context gives the highest performance on most datasets; on Clinic-150 neither LoRA nor full FT beats ICL at the same example count.
results.setup: Llama2-7b with classification head; ICL vs LoRA vs full FT; 30 epochs, best checkpoint chosen on the test set
results.quote: on the dataset with the most labels, Clinic-150, neither LoRA finetuning nor full finetuning ever outperforms ICL at the same number of examples.

results.claim: LoRA finetuning mostly never exceeds long-context ICL.
results.quote: For most datasets, LoRA finetuning performance never exceeds long-context ICL performance even with additional examples

results.claim: Frontier models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 3.1 405B) saturate early on Clinic-150; part of the gain is fewer invalid labels.
results.setup: Clinic-150, 50 to 3000 demonstrations, no constrained decoding, single run
results.quote: at least some of this benefit comes from improved knowledge of the label space (i.e. less invalid labels generated) and performance on this task saturates quite quickly.

results.claim: Saturation point (95% of max accuracy) for Clinic-150 on Llama2-80k is 1000 demos of 2000 that fit.
Banking-77 and Clinic-150 do not saturate in Llama2's 4096-token window (100-162 examples).
results.quote: Banking-77 and Clinic-150 do not saturate within the context window of Llama2 (4096 tokens, which represents between 100-162 in-context examples for these datasets).

results.claim: Copy test: no model copies uniformly correctly from context; accuracy ~98% at 100 examples.

results.claim: Long-context ICL helps mainly through retrieval from the context, not cross-attention among demonstrations.
results.quote: We have also shown that long-context ICL’s effectiveness is largely due to retrieval from the long context during prediction,

results.claim: Li et al. 2024's tasks where long context does not help start near zero or already decline at short context.
results.quote: we observe that the tasks that show this trend either have near-0 performance at short demonstration lengths or also display an inverse performance trend on the short context scale

limits: Mainly open-source 7B models and the Llama-2 family; may not hold across families.
No non-LoRA PEFT methods; T-few not tried.
Mostly classification; care in generalizing to other tasks.
Finetuning checkpoint chosen on the test set, so FT numbers are an upper bound; full-FT hyperparameters not tuned.
Frontier-model run is single-run, unconstrained decoding, one dataset (Clinic-150), saturates early.
Models are mostly not instruction-tuned (Mistral is instruct); no instruction or system prompt used.
Saturation point is not fully explained by label-space size.

terms.definition: the smallest number of examples tested such that performance reaches 95% of the model’s maximum performance
the idea that attention is used to select examples, rather than the model aggregating a complex decision boundary by better contextualizing across examples
